stories.title: The "Hall of Unforgettable"
stories.summary:
Decided to start a new thread, because things, are dead here and it seems like a fun idea.  I saw another poster, possibly joking, lobby for Ryan Fitz to make the HOF.



	 



	I'm usually the guy arguing against dudes getting in, when they might only belong in the Hall of Pretty Good (he's a bit of a stretch for that even).... and its impossible to set aside my blatant obvious bias... but what he did is pretty damn unique. 



	 



	Im not saying he should actually get in, but they should have a separate section for notable/ interesting/ truly unique athletes. Which got me thinking:



	 



	"The Hall of Unforgettable":



	-Bo Jackson



	 



	-Nick Foles - backup to SB Champ



	 



	-Tebow (and anybody who ges inflammed at this one, is proving my point)



	 



	-Matt Flynn -- week 16game, big trade, fat contract



	 



	-Ronnie Brown & 'The Wildcat'



	 



	-Rod “He Hate Me” Smart



	 



	--Jared Lorenzen --- the 300lb QB (probably better suited for CFB H.O.Unforgettable)



	 



	-Scott Norwood & The "Wide Right Rally" at City Hall-- probably my favorite type of entry, bias aside. It would commemorate the rare moment when sports fans were presented with an obvious scapegoat and collectively declined to use him. This was before I was old enough to understand, but truly one of our fans greatest performances....



	 



	1. The exhibit begins with a video of the missed kick by motion sensor, it plays only ONCE!



	 



	2. Visitors move down a tight, Hall with a lower ceiling that's a bit dim/ dreary, and displays National News Headlines attributing the Loss to him.... The sound of the broadcast playing overhead gradually fades out .... and evolves into the sound of a crowd as you move down it



	 



	3. It opens into a new room that "puts you" into the crowd downtown at the next day Rally, " We want Scott! We want Scott!"  fades in...  Footage From That Day & Speech Display, splice in old Buffalo local news broadcasts talking to fans after that, ones that ran on TV after, talking about the Day Buffalo Picked Scott Back Up!!!!!



	 



	Damn, not ashamed to say I gave myself the onion cuts picturing it lol that'd be so sick



	 



	Your turn, who/what ya got?.......



	This is not entirely for 'almost/should've made it' guys... but also notable/interesting/cult following guys

The NFL and CTE latest
stories.summary:
I’m hesitant to post this but it’s relevant. CTE article and study results I found Al-Shaair’s comments particularly interesting.
	 



	I told this story on here before but I have a good friend who was a LB. He was a fringe roster guy / teams guy. He kicked around for 7 seasons. He was like a Buffalo Joe type. He told me a story about his concussions. If I’m remembering correctly he had 7 that he knew about. The hardest hit of his career was not one of them. He was covering a kick and got absolutely lit up. He didn’t see the guy. He started walking to the wrong sideline. One of his teammates grabbed him and directed him to the right place. He had no idea where he was for like 5-10 minutes. He tried to stay away from everyone on the sideline because he didn’t want them to know. Eventually his mind cleared and he finished the game. What he said, and has stuck with me was, “I was a fringe roster guy making about $1M a year. This was towards the end of my career. If I come out, I may never get back out there. I’m the ideal cut candidate at that point. I can be replaced by a rookie and they’d save money. I needed to do everything in my power to never show injury to protect my earnings.” That happens all the time in the NFL.
	 



	Was that the right or wrong decision? There’s no easy answer. In one sense, he was risking his health and future every play. In the other breath, he made enough money in those 7 years, plus his pension, that he never has to work again if he doesn’t want to. He isn’t rich by any means but can give his family a decent life on that. Was it worth it? He’s gone back and forth on that but is adamant that he would do the same thing over.



	 



	This is a topic that we all have strong feelings about. Please remain respectful to other posters as you share your thoughts.

stories.title: SSFC Spotlight: Taylor Huff providing creativity for Bay FC
Davison Igbinosun: The draft day hate was way overblown
stories.summary:
A lot of folks on here were losing their minds when we drafted Davison Igbinosun, and honestly, the reaction was way overly critical.



	 



	I get where the frustration came from initially. If you watched him at Ohio State, the grabby play and the flags would drive fans batty. But look at the actual body of work—the guy put up great stats, and more importantly, his penalties dropped off dramatically in his final college season once he dialed in the technique.



	 



	Everything we’ve seen out of camp and preseason tells me this kid is a pure competitor. Is he going to get flagged sometimes as a rookie? Probably. Is he going to take some lumps adjusting to NFL receivers? Almost certainly. But what you are getting is pure nastiness, legitimate toughness, and a guy who flat out refuses to back down from anyone. He’s got the ideal physical traits and he’s ridiculously sticky in press-man.



	 



	I mentioned this in another thread, but his real value is going to show up on high-leverage downs. When we dial up a blitz on 3rd-and-medium and the DC needs corners who can get in a receiver's face, disrupt the timing, and hold up on an island for 2.2 seconds to let the rush get home, Igbinosun is built for that exact role.



	 



	Yeah, it's just preseason, but you can't teach that kind of edge. I really like what I'm seeing from him so far.
